claim: Estrogen receptor alpha (ERα) is overexpressed in approximately 70% of breast cancers.
source: ERα is overexpressed in approximately 70% of breast cancers and targeted endocrine therapies are given to prevent primary disease metastasis.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about breast cancer epidemiology.

claim: Post-menopausal patients primarily receive aromatase inhibitors, which indirectly inhibits ERα by ablating endogenous estrogens.
source: Post-menopausal patients primarily receive aromatase inhibitors, which indirectly inhibits ERα by ablating endogenous estrogens, and may be given in combination with a CDK 4/6 inhibitor (Burstein et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Burstein et al., 2019, indicating it is based on published literature.

claim: Pre-menopausal patients receive tamoxifen, a selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM), which directly binds to the receptor and reprograms transcription to induce cellular quiescence.
source: Pre-menopausal patients receive tamoxifen, a selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM), which directly binds to the receptor and reprograms transcription to induce cellular quiescence (Maximov et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Maximov et al., 2018.

claim: Approximately 50% of patients present acquired or de novo resistance to endocrine therapies after an average of 5-years.
source: Approximately 50% of patients present acquired or de novo resistance to endocrine therapies after an average of 5-years (Anurag et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Anurag et al., 2018.

claim: Deep genomic sequencing of endocrine-resistant, ER+, and metastatic breast cancers revealed the presence of ESR1 ligand binding domain mutations (ESR1muts) at a rate of approximately 25%.
source: Deep genomic sequencing of endocrine-resistant, ER+, and metastatic breast cancers revealed the presence of ESR1 ligand binding domain mutations (ESR1muts) at a rate of approximately 25% (Toy et al., 2013; Jeselsohn et al., 2014; Robinson et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Toy et al., 2013; Jeselsohn et al., 2014; Robinson et al., 2013.

claim: Y537S (14%) and D538G (36%) are the two most prevalent ESR1 mutations and account for nearly 50% of those identified.
source: Y537S (14%) and D538G (36%) are the two most prevalent mutations and account for nearly 50% of those identified.
evidence: This statement provides specific percentages for mutation prevalence, likely derived from the previously cited genomic sequencing studies.

claim: Both Y537S and D538G mutations, especially Y537S, enable hormone-free transcriptional activity, resistance to inhibition by 4-hydroxytamoxifen (4OHT), and are associated with a more aggressive disease phenotype.
source: Both mutations, especially Y537S, enable hormone-free transcriptional activity, resistance to inhibition by 4-hydroxytamoxifen (4OHT, the active metabolite of tamoxifen), and are associated with a more aggressive disease phenotype (Chandarlapaty et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Chandarlapaty et al., 2016.

claim: ESR1 mutations have been identified in cultured breast cancer cells and become enriched as they become resistant to endocrine therapies.
source: ESR1muts have also been identified in cultured breast cancer cells and become enriched as they become resistant to endocrine therapies, suggesting a latent and selectable mechanism of acquired drug resistance (Martin et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Martin et al., 2017.

claim: ESR1 mutations bind to unique cistromes and promote allele-specific transcriptional programs compared to E2-stimulated WT receptor.
source: In addition to mimicking the genomic actions of E2 stimulation, ESR1muts bind to unique cistromes and promote allele-specific transcriptional programs compared to E2-stimulated WT receptor (Jeselsohn et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Jeselsohn et al., 2018.

claim: Y537S and D538G mutations favor an E2-like agonist conformation in the absence of hormone.
source: Biochemical studies and x-ray crystal structures have shown that both mutations favor an E2-like agonist conformation in the absence of hormone (Fanning et al., 2016; Nettles et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Fanning et al., 2016 and Nettles et al., 2008.

claim: The favored agonist conformation reduces the binding affinity of ERα ligands and alters the therapeutically important antagonist receptor conformation of the SERM 4OHT.
source: This favored agonist conformation reduces the binding affinity of ERα ligands and alters the therapeutically important antagonist receptor conformation of the SERM 4OHT (Fanning et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Fanning et al., 2016.

claim: Competitive antiestrogens with SERD activities show superior therapeutic antagonistic activities compared to 4OHT in breast cancer cells harboring Y537S or D538G ESR1.
source: Competitive antiestrogens with selective estrogen receptor degrader/downregulator (SERD) activities with improved potencies show superior therapeutic antagonistic activities compared to 4OHT in breast cancer cells harboring Y537S or D538G ESR1 (Fanning et al., 2018b).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Fanning et al., 2018b.

claim: Fulvestrant completely ablated Y537S ERα transcriptional activity in breast cancer cells.
source: The SERD fulvestrant, contrary to 4OHT, completely ablated Y537S ERα transcriptional activity in breast cancer cells (Toy et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Toy et al., 2013.

claim: Fulvestrant's antiestrogenicity stems from its ability to antagonize ERα transcription and reduce its cellular lifetime by inducing post-translational modifications including SUMOylation and ubiquitination.
source: Fulvestrant's antiestrogenicity stems from its ability to antagonize ERα transcription and reduce its cellular lifetime (degrade/downregulate receptor) by inducing post-translational modifications including SUMOylation and ubiquitination by increasing proteasomal degradation (Wijayaratne and McDonnell, 2001; Traboulsi et al., 2019; Hilmi et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Wijayaratne and McDonnell, 2001; Traboulsi et al., 2019; Hilmi et al., 2012.

claim: Tamoxifen and other SERMs antagonize transcription but induce a stable antagonist conformation that enhances ERα nuclear lifetime.
source: Tamoxifen and other SERMs also antagonize transcription but induce a stable antagonist conformation that enhances ERα nuclear lifetime (Fanning et al., 2018b).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Fanning et al., 2018b.

claim: SERMs show partial agonist activities in the uterine endometrium and/or in bone while SERDs are pure antagonists.
source: SERMs show partial agonist activities in the uterine endometrium and/or in bone while SERDs are pure antagonists (Fanning and Greene, 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Fanning and Greene, 2019.

claim: Recent studies suggest that ERα degrading activities may not be required for therapeutic efficacy in breast cancer cells with recurring hotspot ESR1 mutations.
source: Interestingly, recent studies suggest that ERα degrading activities may not be required for therapeutic efficacy in breast cancer cells with recurring hotspot ESR1 mutations (Fanning et al., 2018b; Lainé et al., 2021; Wardell et al., 2015a; Andreano et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Fanning et al., 2018b; Lainé et al., 2021; Wardell et al., 2015a; Andreano et al., 2020.

claim: A series of methylpyrollidine lasofoxifene derivatives were developed that maintained the drug's antagonistic activities while uniquely tuning ERα cellular accumulation.
source: To understand whether chemical manipulation of ERα cellular lifetime and accumulation influences antagonistic activity, we studied a series of methylpyrollidine lasofoxifene (Laso) derivatives that maintained the drug's antagonistic activities while uniquely tuning ERα cellular accumulation.
evidence: This is a statement of the study's experimental approach and findings.

claim: Molecules that favor a highly buried helix 12 antagonist conformation achieve the greatest transcriptional suppression activities in breast cancer cells harboring WT/Y537S ESR1.
source: High-resolution x-ray crystal structures of WT and Y537S ERα ligand binding domain in complex with the methylated Laso derivatives or representative SERMs and SERDs show that molecules that favor a highly buried helix 12 antagonist conformation achieve the greatest transcriptional suppression activities in breast cancer cells harboring WT/Y537S ESR1.
evidence: This statement is based on x-ray crystal structure data and transcriptional assays presented in the manuscript.

claim: Chemical reduction of ERα cellular lifetime is not necessarily the most crucial parameter for transcriptional antagonism in ESR1 mutated breast cancer cells.
source: Together these results show that chemical reduction of ERα cellular lifetime is not necessarily the most crucial parameter for transcriptional antagonism in ESR1 mutated breast cancer cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the study.

claim: Small chemical differences within a scaffold series can provide compounds with similar antagonistic activities, but with greatly different effects on the cellular lifetime of the ERα.
source: Importantly, our studies show how small chemical differences within a scaffold series can provide compounds with similar antagonistic activities, but with greatly different effects of the cellular lifetime of the ERα, which is crucial for achieving desired SERM or SERD profiles.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the study.

claim: T47D breast cancer cells were engineered to express a doxycycline (dox) inducible halo-tagged (HT) ERα.
source: T47D breast cancer cells were engineered to express a doxycycline (dox) inducible halo-tagged (HT) ERα, allowing the cells to be treated with a permeable HT-specific fluorophore (halo-618) and levels of ERα expression quantified following the addition of dox.
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology used in the study.

claim: 1 μg/mL doxycycline was the lowest dose needed to achieve maximal signal-to-noise ratio in the halo-ERα expression assay.
source: Using a range of dox concentrations, we found that 1 μg/mL was the lowest dose needed to achieve maximal signal-to-noise ratio (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: For WT cells, ERα reached a maximum at approximately 24 hr then fell to baseline by 80 hr.
source: For WT cells, ERα reached a maximum at approximately 24 hr then fell to baseline by 80 hr (Figure 2A).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Treatment with SERDs reduced ERα signal and led to a rapid return to baseline, at around 45 hr for fulvestrant in WT cells.
source: Treatment with SERDs further reduced the signal and led to a rapid return to baseline, at around 45 hr for fulvestrant (Figure 2A).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Treatment with SERMs greatly enhanced ERα levels over vehicle and extended the time to baseline to past 80 hr in WT cells.
source: Treatment with SERMs greatly enhanced ERα levels over vehicle and extended the time to baseline to past 80 hr (Figure 2D).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Vehicle-treated WT and Y537S cells showed similar ERα expression profiles, but the Y537S mutant took slightly longer to reach baseline.
source: Interestingly, veh-treated WT and Y537S cells showed similar profiles, but the Y537S mutant took slightly longer to reach baseline (Figure 2B).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: E2-treated Y537S cells showed an identical pattern to veh-treated Y537S cells, unlike E2-treated WT cells.
source: Unlike the E2-treated WT cells, E2-treated Y537S cells showed an identical pattern to veh-treated Y537S cells (Figure 2B).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The Y537S mutant extended the ERα lifetime in the presence of fulvestrant, past 60 hr compared to 45 hr for WT.
source: Surprisingly, the Y537S mutant extended the ERα lifetime in the presence of fulvestrant, past 60 hr compared to 45 hr for WT (Figure 2B).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The D538G mutant reduced the magnitude of ERα expression and the kinetics of its cellular turnover with a greater time to baseline for each SERD.
source: Unexpectedly, the D538G mutant not only reduced the magnitude of ERα expression, but also the kinetics of its cellular turnover with a greater time to baseline for each SERD (Figure 2C).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: RU39411 was the only SERM to elicit any kind of difference on D538G by showing a slight increase in stability.
source: Surprisingly, RU39411 was the only SERM to elicit any kind of difference on D538G by showing a slight increase in stability; however, it was still approximately 2.5-fold less than in the Y537S (Figure 2F).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Y537S and D538G mutations uniquely affect ERα cellular lifetime within T47D cells.
source: These data suggest that, in addition to hormone independent transcriptional activities, both Y537S and D538G mutations uniquely affect ERα cellular lifetime within T47D cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on ERα lifetime in mutant cells.

claim: GDC-0927, fulvestrant, and pipendoxifene showed the most potent IC50 values at 0.13 ± 0.03, 0.4 ± 0.02, and 0.77 ± 0.03 nM for WT ERα degradation.
source: Overall, GDC-0927, fulvestrant, and pipendoxifene (PIP) showed the most potent IC50 values at 0.13 ± 0.03, 0.4 ± 0.02, and 0.77 ± 0.03 nM.
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from the ERα degradation assays.

claim: SERM-like molecules retained their abilities to increase receptor nuclear lifetime in the Y537S, but did so with approximately 10-fold reduced IC50 values.
source: SERM-like molecules appeared to retain their abilities to increase receptor nuclear lifetime in the Y537S, but did so with approximately 10-fold reduced IC50 values (Figure 2H and Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2H and Figure 2—source data 1.

claim: Laso showed a SERM-like profile with Y537S with a normalized fluorescence of 1.48 ± 0.22 at 5 μM.
source: Laso, which was essentially neutral to slightly SERD-like in the WT cells, showed a SERM-like profile with Y537S (1.48 ± 0.22 at 5 μM).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from the ERα degradation assays.

claim: SERD molecules that possessed carboxylic acids (AZD9496, LSZ102, and GDC0801) all showed more SERM-like profiles with Y537S.
source: Interestingly, SERD molecules that possessed carboxylic acids (AZD9496, LSZ102, and GDC0801) all showed more SERM-like profiles with their normalized fluorescence above 1 at 5 μM.
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from the ERα degradation assays.

claim: The D538G mutation mostly abolished ligand-dependent control on receptor levels.
source: Surprisingly, introduction of the D538G mutation mostly abolished ligand-dependent control on receptor levels (Figure 2I).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2I.

claim: GDC-0927 was the only SERD that attained maximal effect on normalized fluorescence with an IC50 <10 nM at 1.88 ±0.04 nM for D538G.
source: GDC-0927 was the only SERD that attained maximal effect on normalized fluorescence with an IC50 <10 nM at 1.88 ±0.04 nM.
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from the ERα degradation assays with D538G.

claim: LA-3 possesses a 3R methylpyrrolidine and showed a SERD-like profile with an IC50 of 26.94 ± 0.4 nM and maximum normalized fluorescence of 0.48 ± 0.07 at 5 μM.
source: LA-3 possesses a 3 R methylpyrrolidine (similar to OP1074) and showed a SERD-like profile with an IC50 of 26.94 ± 0.4 nM and maximum normalized fluorescence of 0.48 ± 0.07 at 5 μM.
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from the ERα degradation assays with the synthesized Laso derivatives.

claim: LA-5 possesses a 2S methylpyrrolidine and showed a SERM-like profile with an IC50 of 15.68+0.27 nM and a normalized fluorescence of 1.706 ± 0.09 at 5 μM.
source: LA-5 possesses a 2 S methylpyrrolidine and showed a SERM-like profile with an IC50 of 15.68+0.27 nM and a normalized fluorescence of 1.706 ± 0.09 at 5 μM.
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from the ERα degradation assays with the synthesized Laso derivatives.

claim: LA2 and LA4 appeared similar to Laso in that they did not affect receptor lifetime.
source: LA2 and LA4 appeared similar to Laso in that they did not affect receptor lifetime.
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from the ERα degradation assays with the synthesized Laso derivatives.

claim: Chiral separation substantially improved the IC50 but not the fluorescence at maximum dose for LA3 and LA5.
source: As such, chiral separation substantially improved the IC50 but not the fluorescence at maximum dose.
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from the chiral separation and subsequent assays.

claim: LA-Stab demonstrated a slightly improved IC50 over 4OHT at 10.62 ± 0.12 and 12.42 ± 0.15 nM respectively in Y537S cells.
source: In Y537S cells, LA-Stab demonstrated a slightly improved IC50 over 4OHT at 10.62 ± 0.12 and 12.42 ± 0.15 nM respectively.
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from the ERα degradation assays with Y537S cells.

claim: The Y537S mutation essentially neutralized the SERD activities of LA-Deg with a normalized fluorescence of 1.01 ± 0.04 at 5 μM.
source: Interestingly, the Y537S essentially neutralized the SERD activities of LA-Deg with a normalized fluorescence of 1.01 ± 0.04 at 5 μM.
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from the ERα degradation assays with Y537S cells.

claim: Fulvestrant induces both ubiquitination and SUMOylation of ERα in breast cancer cells, impacting its stability and activity.
source: Fulvestrant induces both ubiquitination and SUMOylation of ERα in breast cancer cells, impacting its stability and activity (Hilmi et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Hilmi et al., 2012.

claim: In both WT and Y537S cells, fulvestrant induces the greatest degree of SUMO3 recruitment, but the IC50 values and maximum BRET ratios are decreased with the Y537S mutant.
source: In both WT and Y537S cells, fulvestrant induces the greatest degree of SUMO3 recruitment, but the IC50 values and maximum BRET ratios are decreased with the Y537S mutant.
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from the SUMO BRET assays.

claim: GDC0927 is the next most efficacious antiestrogen for inducing SUMOylation and its potency trends similarly to fulvestrant with the Y537S mutant.
source: GDC0927 is the next most efficacious antiestrogen and its potency trends similarly to fulvestrant with the Y537S mutant.
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from the SUMO BRET assays.

claim: LA-Deg induces SUMOylation but to a lesser maximum than fulvestrant and GDC0927 in WT and is further reduced in Y537S.
source: LA-Deg induces SUMOylation but to a lesser maximum than fulvestrant and GDC0927 in WT and is further reduced in Y537S, while LA-Stab did not induce SUMOylation with either receptor.
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from the SUMO BRET assays.

claim: LA-Stab did not induce SUMOylation with either WT or Y537S receptor.
source: LA-Deg induces SUMOylation but to a lesser maximum than fulvestrant and GDC0927 in WT and is further reduced in Y537S, while LA-Stab did not induce SUMOylation with either receptor.
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from the SUMO BRET assays.

claim: RAL showed weak SERD-like activity in WT but not mutant ERα in cellular lifetime and accumulation assays, and also induced low levels of SUMOylation in the WT but not the Y537S cells.
source: Interestingly, RAL, which showed weak SERD-like activity in WT but not mutant ERα in our cellular lifetime and accumulation assays, also induced low levels of SUMOylation in the WT but not the Y537S cells.
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from the cellular lifetime and SUMO BRET assays.

claim: There is a correlation between a molecule's ERα-degrading activities and induction of SUMOylation.
source: Overall, these assays show a correlation between a molecule's ERα-degrading activities and induction of SUMOylation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on ERα degradation and SUMOylation.

claim: The acrylic acid SERD AZD9496 did not induce SUMOylation with any ERα construct.
source: However, the acrylic acid SERD AZD9496 did not induce SUMOylation with any ERα construct.
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from the SUMO BRET assays.

claim: The D538G mutant showed the greatest alterations in induced SUMOylation compared to WT and Y537S ERα in the BRET assay.
source: As in our cellular lifetime studies, the D538G mutant showed the greatest alterations in induced SUMOylation compared to WT and Y537S ERα in the BRET assay.
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from the SUMO BRET assays.

claim: Fulvestrant induced about 25% of the SUMOylation for D538G compared to WT ERα.
source: Fulvestrant induced about 25% of the SUMOylation for D538G compared to WT ERα.
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from the SUMO BRET assays.

claim: GDC0927 was less affected in its capacity to induce SUMOylation by D538G, albeit its potency was reduced.
source: GDC0927 was less affected in its capacity to induce SUMOylation by D538G, albeit its potency was reduced, consistent with our lifetime/accumulation experiments.
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from the SUMO BRET assays.

claim: LA-Stab and LA-Deg displayed similar SUMOylation activity with D538G, contrary to observations with WT and Y537S ERα.
source: Surprisingly, LA-Stab and LA-Deg displayed similar activity, contrary to observations with WT and Y537S ERα.
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from the SUMO BRET assays.

claim: 4OHT induced low levels of SUMOylation in the D538G mutant that were not observed for WT and Y537S.
source: Interestingly, 4OHT also induced low levels of SUMOylation in the D538G mutant that were not observed for WT and Y537S.
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from the SUMO BRET assays.

claim: The D538G activating somatic ESR1 mutation uniquely affects receptor SUMOylation in response to SERDs.
source: Together, these studies show that the D538G activating somatic ESR1 mutation uniquely affects receptor SUMOylation in response to SERDs, in agreement with our measured differences in cellular lifetime.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on SUMOylation and cellular lifetime.

claim: Enhanced basal BRET ratios are observed for the Y537S and D538G mutants compared to WT ERα in coactivator binding assays.
source: Overall, enhanced basal BRET ratios are observed for the mutants compared to WT ERα.
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from the BRET coactivator binding assays.

claim: The Y537S and D538G mutations decreased the potencies of all SERMs and SERDs to inhibit coactivator binding.
source: The mutations also decreased the potencies of all SERMs and SERDs to inhibit coactivator binding, consistent with earlier findings for 4OHT and bazedoxifene (BZA) using purified recombinant proteins in vitro (Fanning et al., 2018b).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from the BRET coactivator binding assays and is consistent with prior published findings.

claim: All molecules showed similar efficacies in inhibiting SRC1 RID interaction at the greatest concentrations.
source: Interestingly, all molecules showed similar efficacies in inhibiting this interaction at the greatest concentrations.
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from the BRET coactivator binding assays.

claim: AZD9496 showed the greatest potency for inhibiting SRC1 RID binding for all ERα species, but is approximately 10-fold reduced in the mutants.
source: AZD9496 showed the greatest potency for all ERα species, but is approximately 10-fold reduced in the mutants.
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from the BRET coactivator binding assays.

claim: Induction of ERα SUMOylation does not correlate with repression of SRC1 RID recruitment in cells.
source: Because SERDs showed varied potencies in prohibiting coactivator association with the ERα mutants and did not display greater efficacies, we conclude that induction of ERα SUMOylation does not correlate with repression of SRC1 RID recruitment in cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on SUMOylation and coactivator binding.

claim: GDC0927, RAL, and OP1074 showed the most potent transcriptional inhibition in WT MCF7 cells at IC50 = 0.03 ± 0.08, 0.11 ± 0.08, and 0.14 ± 0.05 nM respectively.
source: For WT cells: GDC0927, RAL, and OP1074 showed the most potent transcriptional inhibition at IC50 = 0.03 ± 0.08, 0.11 ± 0.08, and 0.14 ± 0.05 nM respectively, compared to 0.35 ± 0.06 nM for fulvestrant (Figure 5D and G).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from the transcriptional reporter gene assays shown in Figure 5D and G.

claim: At the 5 μM maximum dose, RU39411, RAL, and BZA showed the greatest reduction in transcription at 0.14 ± 0.02, 0.16 ± 0.02, and 0.17 ± 0.01 in WT MCF7 cells.
source: At the 5 μM maximum dose, RU39411, RAL, and BZA showed the greatest reduction in transcription at 0.14 ± 0.02, 0.16 ± 0.02, and 0.17 ± 0.01.
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from the transcriptional reporter gene assays.

claim: In the WT/Y537S heterozygous cells GDC0927, RAL, and Laso showed the most potent inhibition at IC50 = 0.95 ± 0.51, 2.16 ± 0.67, and 2.88 ± 0.34 nM respectively.
source: In the WT/Y537S heterozygous cells GDC0927, RAL, and Laso showed the most potent inhibition at IC50 = 0.95 ± 0.51, 2.16 ± 0.67, and 2.88 ± 0.34 nM respectively.
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from the transcriptional reporter gene assays.

claim: At the maximum dose, RU39411, BZA, and PIP showed the greatest reduction in transcription at 0.33 ± 0.02, 0.32 ± 0.05, and 0.32 ± 0.04 respectively in WT/Y537S heterozygous cells.
source: At the maximum dose: RU39411, BZA, and PIP showed the greatest reduction in transcription at 0.33 ± 0.02, 0.32 ± 0.05, and 0.32 ± 0.04 respectively.
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from the transcriptional reporter gene assays.

claim: No antiestrogen completely reduced transcriptional activity in cells that possessed Y537S ERα.
source: As previously reported, no antiestrogen completely reduced transcriptional activity in cells that possessed Y537S ERα (Toy et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from the transcriptional reporter gene assays and is consistent with prior published findings.

claim: In the WT/D538G heterozygous cells RU39411, fulvestrant, and OP-1074 showed the best IC50 values at 0.26 ± 0.53, 0.57 ± 0.69, and 0.52 ± 0.63 nM respectively.
source: In the WT/D538G heterozygous cells RU39411, fulvestrant, and OP-1074 showed the best IC50 values at 0.26 ± 0.53, 0.57 ± 0.69, and 0.52 ± 0.63 nM respectively.
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from the transcriptional reporter gene assays.

claim: At the maximum dose, OP1154, PIP, fulvestrant, and OP1074 showed the greatest transcriptional inhibition at normalized fluorescence of 0.25 ± 0.03, 0.29 ± 0.07, 0.32 ± 0.03, and 0.37±0.05 respectively in WT/D538G heterozygous cells.
source: At the maximum dose: OP1154, PIP, fulvestrant, and OP1074 showed the greatest transcriptional inhibition at normalized fluorescence of 0.25 ± 0.03, 0.29 ± 0.07, 0.32 ± 0.03, and 0.37±0.05 respectively.
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from the transcriptional reporter gene assays.

claim: Only OP1154, PIP, fulvestrant, and OP1074 returned the D538G transcriptional activity back to their respective WT values.
source: Only these four molecules returned the D538G transcriptional activity back to their respective WT values.
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from the transcriptional reporter gene assays.

claim: Neither the potency nor the efficacy of induced ERα degradation correlate with improved transcriptional inhibition for the Y537S and D538G mutant receptors.
source: Together, these data suggest that neither the potency nor the efficacy of induced ERα degradation correlate with improved transcriptional inhibition for the Y537S and D538G mutant receptors in this assay.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on ERα degradation and transcriptional inhibition.

claim: 1 nM E2 induced the greatest alkaline phosphatase response in Ishikawa cells followed by LA-Stab, 4OHT, Z-endoxifen, and Laso.
source: 1 nM E2 induced the greatest AP response followed by LA-Stab, 4OHT, Z-endoxifen, and Laso.
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from the alkaline phosphatase assays.

claim: LA-Deg showed a slightly increased alkaline phosphatase induction compared to ICI and Veh, but it was significantly lower than Laso.
source: LA-Deg showed a slightly increase induction compared to ICI and Veh, but it was significantly lower than Laso.
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from the alkaline phosphatase assays.

claim: The SERM-like effects on ERα accumulation observed for LA-Stab correlate to an increased stimulation of ERα-activities in uterine cells.
source: Together, these data suggest that the SERM-like effects on ERα accumulation observed for LA-Stab correlate to an increased stimulation of ERα-activities in uterine cells, while, modest ERα-degradation by LA-Deg was sufficient to prevent uterine stimulation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on ERα accumulation and alkaline phosphatase activity.

claim: Modest ERα-degradation by LA-Deg was sufficient to prevent uterine stimulation.
source: Together, these data suggest that the SERM-like effects on ERα accumulation observed for LA-Stab correlate to an increased stimulation of ERα-activities in uterine cells, while, modest ERα-degradation by LA-Deg was sufficient to prevent uterine stimulation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on ERα degradation and alkaline phosphatase activity.

claim: No compound completely abrogated proliferation in MCF7 WT/Y537S cells, even at the highest dose.
source: No compound completely abrogated proliferation, even at the highest dose.
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from the cellular proliferation assays.

claim: Every compound shows similar efficacies at the maximum 1 μM dose in MCF7 WT/Y537S cells, although LA-Deg and LA-Stab appear slightly improved and closest to veh levels.
source: Every compound shows similar efficacies at the maximum 1 μM dose, although LA-Deg and LA-Stab appear slightly improved and closest to veh levels.
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from the cellular proliferation assays.

claim: Differences in anti-proliferative efficacy were not statistically significant compared to the other molecules at the maximal dose in MCF7 WT/Y537S cells.
source: However, differences were not statistically significant compared to the other molecules at the maximal dose.
evidence: This statement is based on statistical analysis of experimental data from the cellular proliferation assays.

claim: Fulvestrant and Laso show improved efficacies at the 1 nM and 50 nM doses compared to the other molecules in MCF7 WT/Y537S cells.
source: Fulvestrant and Laso on the other hand show improved efficacies at the 1 nM and 50 nM doses compared to the other molecules.
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from the cellular proliferation assays.

claim: Induction of ERα degradation does not by itself predict the anti-proliferative activities of an antiestrogen in MCF7 WT/Y537S cells.
source: Together, these data show that induction of ERα degradation does not by itself predict the anti-proliferative activities of an antiestrogen in this cell model.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on ERα degradation and cellular proliferation.

claim: X-ray crystal structures were solved for BZA, RAL, 4OHT, LA-Deg, LA-Stab, RU39411 and LSZ102 in complex with the Y537S mutant ERα LBD.
source: We solved x-ray crystal structures for BZA, RAL, 4OHT, LA-Deg, LA-Stab, RU39411 and LSZ102 in complex with the Y537S mutant.
evidence: This describes the structural biology experiments performed in the study.

claim: X-ray crystal structures were solved with the WT LBD for LA-Deg, LA-Stab, RU39411 and RAL (improved resolution).
source: We also solved structures with the WT LBD for those molecules with no existing structures (LA-Deg, LA-Stab, RU39411) or were able to solve to improved resolution (RAL).
evidence: This describes the structural biology experiments performed in the study.

claim: The authors were unable to solve x-ray crystal structures for antagonists in complex with the D538G mutant.
source: We were unable to solve x-ray crystal structures for antagonists in complex with the D538G mutant, despite earlier success with 4OHT (Jeselsohn et al., 2018).
evidence: This describes the limitations of the structural biology experiments.

claim: In the most effective molecules (BZA, RAL, and RU39411), H12 maintains a conserved AF-2 antagonist conformation that is well ordered in the AF2 cleft regardless of mutation.
source: In the most effective molecules (BZA, RAL, and RU39411), superposition of all monomers of WT and Y537S structures, based on alpha carbon positions, shows that H12 maintains a conserved AF-2 antagonist conformation that is well ordered in the AF2 cleft regardless of mutation (Figure 8A/B).
evidence: This statement is based on analysis of x-ray crystal structure data shown in Figure 8A/B.

claim: A new hydrogen bond is observed between S537 and E380 in Y537S structures with the most effective molecules.
source: In addition, a new hydrogen bond is observed between S537 and E380 (Figure 8C), which was previously computationally predicted for the Y537S-BZA structure (Fanning et al., 2018b).
evidence: This statement is based on analysis of x-ray crystal structure data shown in Figure 8C and is consistent with prior computational predictions.

claim: In Laso, LA-Stab, and LA-Deg Y537S structures, H12 is slightly more dynamic and the S537-E380 hydrogen bond is no longer observed.
source: Laso, LA-Stab, and LA-Deg showed intermediate efficacy. In these Y537S structures, H12 is slightly more dynamic and the S537-E380 hydrogen bond is no longer observed.
evidence: This statement is based on analysis of x-ray crystal structure data.

claim: 4OHT and LSZ102 show significant Y537S H12 conformational changes, are significantly less ordered in the AF2 cleft, and no S537-E380 hydrogen bond is observed.
source: 4OHT and LSZ102 were the least effective molecules. Both show significant Y537S H12 conformational changes, are significantly less ordered in the AF2 cleft, and no S537-E380 hydrogen bond is observed (Figure 8D–F).
evidence: This statement is based on analysis of x-ray crystal structure data shown in Figure 8D–F.

claim: The least effective molecules (4OHT and LSZ102) possess greater main-chain H12 B-factors indicating a relatively poor packing in the AF-2 cleft compared to more effective molecules.
source: Indeed, the least effective molecules (4OHT and LSZ102) possess greater main-chain H12 B-factors (normalized to all main chain atoms) indicating a relatively poor packing in the AF-2 cleft compared to more effective molecules (Figure 8—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This statement is based on B-factor analysis of x-ray crystal structure data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 2.

claim: H12 buried surface area (BSA) in Y537S LBD correlates with transcriptional antagonism.
source: We further calculated H12 buried surface area (BSA) Y537S LBD using proteins, interfaces, structures, and assemblies (Krissinel and Henrick, 2005) and found it correlates with transcriptional antagonism.
evidence: This statement is based on analysis of x-ray crystal structure data and transcriptional assay data.

claim: BZA, RAL, and RU39411 show the greatest H12 buried surface area at 379.75, 377.87, and 325.21 Å² respectively in Y537S structures.
source: BZA, RAL, and RU39411 show the greatest burial at 379.75, 377.87, and 325.21 Å (Maximov et al., 2018) respectively.
evidence: This statement is based on buried surface area calculations from x-ray crystal structure data.

claim: Molecules with reduced potencies showed reduced H12 buried surface area at 245.57, 56.13, 27.62, and 14.69 Å² for LA-Stab, LSZ-102, LA-Deg, and 4OHT respectively in Y537S structures.
source: Molecules with reduced potencies showed reduced BSA at 245.57, 56.13, 27.62, and 14.69 Å (Maximov et al., 2018) for LA-Stab, LSZ-102, LA-Deg, and 4OHT respectively.
evidence: This statement is based on buried surface area calculations from x-ray crystal structure data.

claim: SERMs, SERM/SERDs, or SERDs that favor H12 packing in the AF-2 cleft and promote an S537-E380 hydrogen bond achieve the greatest anti-transcriptional efficacies in MCF7 breast cancer cells that harbor WT/Y537S ERα.
source: Together these structures show that SERMs, SERM/SERDs, or SERDs that favor H12 packing in the AF-2 cleft and promote an S537-E380 hydrogen bond and achieve the greatest anti-transcriptional efficacies in MCF7 breast cancer cells that harbor WT/Y537S ERα.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the x-ray crystal structure data and transcriptional assay data.

claim: SERMs extend ERα lifetime, increase receptor accumulation, and are antagonists in the breast and agonists in the bone and uterine epithelium.
source: SERMs extend ERα lifetime, increase receptor accumulation, and are antagonists in the breast and agonists in the bone and uterine epithelium (Fanning and Greene, 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Fanning and Greene, 2019.

claim: Tissue-specific partial agonist activities of SERMs stem from SERM inhibition of Activating Function-2 (AF-2) but not AF-1 genomic activities.
source: Tissue-specific partial agonist activities stem from SERM inhibition of Activating Function-2 (AF-2) but not AF-1 genomic activities (Shang and Brown, 2002).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Shang and Brown, 2002.

claim: SERDs decrease the quantity and lifetime of ERα in the cell and are pure antagonists by effectively prohibiting ERα transcriptional activities.
source: SERDs decrease the quantity and lifetime of ERα in the cell and are pure antagonists by effectively prohibiting ERα transcriptional activities.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about SERDs.

claim: Laso induced marked anti-cancer activities in xenografts of Y537S ESR1 breast cancer cells without fulvestrant-level ERα degradation.
source: Initial studies suggested that SERD activity was necessary for therapeutic potency (Toy et al., 2013); however, Lainé et al. showed that the SERM Laso induced marked anti-cancer activities in xenografts of Y537S ESR1 breast cancer cells without fulvestrant-level ERα degradation (Lainé et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Lainé et al., 2021.

claim: Antagonism rather than ERα degradation/downregulation drives most of fulvestrant efficacy in suppressing primary tumor growth in xenograft assays.
source: In addition, Wardell et al., 2020 concluded that antagonism rather than ERα degradation/downregulation drives most of fulvestrant efficacy in suppressing primary tumor growth in xenograft assays, based on observations that a dose of fulvestrant affording a non-significant reduction in ER levels led to significant growth suppression of a long-term estrogen-deprived breast cancer cell model over 4 weeks ().
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Wardell et al., 2020.

claim: Fulvestrant retains transcriptional inhibition properties upon increases in ERα concentrations that lead to saturation of degradation.
source: This is supported by observation in cell lines that fulvestrant retains transcriptional inhibition properties upon increases in ERα concentrations that lead to saturation of degradation. (Lupien et al., 2007)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Lupien et al., 2007.

claim: Addition of a 3R-methyl group on Laso's pyrrolidine induced both ERα SUMOylation and degrading activities.
source: We discovered that addition of a 3R-methyl group on Laso's pyrrolidine induced both ERα SUMOylation and degrading activities, while addition of a 2S-methyl on the pyrrolidine leads to an accumulation of ERα in the breast cancer cells.
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from the study.

claim: Addition of a 2S-methyl on Laso's pyrrolidine leads to an accumulation of ERα in the breast cancer cells.
source: We discovered that addition of a 3R-methyl group on Laso's pyrrolidine induced both ERα SUMOylation and degrading activities, while addition of a 2S-methyl on the pyrrolidine leads to an accumulation of ERα in the breast cancer cells.
evidence: This statement is based on experimental data from the study.

claim: The Y537S mutant likely contributes to breast cancer pathology through increasing the quantity of active receptor in the cell.
source: In addition to constitutive transcriptional activities and resistance to inhibition by tamoxifen, the Y537S also likely contributes to breast cancer pathology through increasing the quantity of active receptor in the cell.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data on Y537S ERα expression.

claim: The diminished ability of cells to degrade D538G ERα coupled with its low-level constitutive transcriptional activities contributes a pathological advantage within the tumor in the presence of first-line endocrine therapies.
source: Our studies suggest that the diminished ability of cells to degrade D538G ERα coupled with its low-level constitutive transcriptional activities contributes a pathological advantage within the tumor in the presence of first-line endocrine therapies.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data on D538G ERα degradation and activity.

claim: SERM or SERD influences on ERα cellular lifetime may not directly correlate with transcriptional antagonistic and anti-proliferative activities of ESR1 mutant breast cancer cells.
source: Together, these data suggest that SERM or SERD influences on ERα cellular lifetime may not directly correlate with transcriptional antagonistic and anti-proliferative activities of ESR1 mutant breast cancer cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on ERα lifetime, transcriptional activity, and proliferation.

claim: Engineered chemical reduction of ERα cellular accumulation is critical for tuning tissue- and gene-specific agonistic/partial agonistic activities.
source: Rather, engineered chemical reduction of ERα cellular accumulation is critical for tuning tissue- and gene-specific agonistic/partial agonistic activities (Fanning and Greene, 2019) and preventing AF-1 dependent mechanisms of endocrine resistance (Massarweh et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Fanning and Greene, 2019 and Massarweh et al., 2008.

claim: Engineered chemical reduction of ERα cellular accumulation is critical for preventing AF-1 dependent mechanisms of endocrine resistance.
source: Rather, engineered chemical reduction of ERα cellular accumulation is critical for tuning tissue- and gene-specific agonistic/partial agonistic activities (Fanning and Greene, 2019) and preventing AF-1 dependent mechanisms of endocrine resistance (Massarweh et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Fanning and Greene, 2019 and Massarweh et al., 2008.

claim: ERα proteolysis is critical to normal activity and E2 binding induces phosphorylation at position Y537, which recruits E3 ubiquitin ligases.
source: ERα proteolysis is critical to normal activity and E2 binding induces phosphorylation at position Y537, which recruits E3 ubiquitin ligases (Sun et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Sun et al., 2012.

claim: SERDs, like fulvestrant, increase H12 conformational mobility and enhance binding of corepressor proteins such as NCOR that are important contributors to anti-cancer activities.
source: SERDs, like fulvestrant, increase H12 conformational mobility (Fanning et al., 2018b; Pike et al., 2001) and enhance binding of corepressor proteins such as NCOR (Webb et al., 2003) that are important contributors to anti-cancer activities.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Fanning et al., 2018b; Pike et al., 2001; and Webb et al., 2003.

claim: It is likely that SERMs and SERDs differentially affect the repertoire of coregulator proteins that associate with Y537S ERα and contribute to anti-cancer activities.
source: Therefore, it is likely that SERMs and SERDs differentially affect the repertoire of coregulator proteins that associate with Y537S ERα and contribute to anti-cancer activities.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the experimental findings and prior knowledge.
